translationRepairs: At seventeen Tan met Qi's Emperor Wu serving as Central Army commander; he was made a retainer, then chief clerk.
At seventeen, when Emperor Wu of Qi was Central Army commander, Tan was appointed a retainer, then transferred to chief clerk.
命爲參軍 is an appointment order, not a meeting; 'met' invents an encounter absent from 惔年十七，齊武帝爲中軍，命爲參軍，轉主簿, and the proposed wording restores the appointment and transfer.
Early in Qi he entered the secretariat as three-ducal attendant, rose to crown prince gentleman companion, and befriended the Prince of Badong, Zi Xiang.
Early in Qi he entered the secretariat as three-ducal attendant, rose to crown prince gentleman companion, and was made Friend of the Prince of Badong, Zi Xiang.
巴東王子響友 continues the office sequence after 太子中舍人; 友 is the princely household office 'Friend', not a social 'befriended' relationship.
Early in Qi he entered the Masters of Writing as attendant of the Three Ducal Officials, rose through posts to crown prince gentleman companion, and became a friend of the Prince of Badong, Zi Xiang.
Early in Qi he entered the Masters of Writing as attendant of the Three Ducal Officials, rose through posts to crown prince gentleman companion, and became Friend of the Prince of Badong, Zi Xiang.
In the same office chain, 友 is the title Friend of the prince; capitalizing Friend correctly marks the office rather than ordinary friendship.
When Ying fell, Yingzhou wanted to move the capital to Xiakou; Chen argued again that Ba and the gorges were not yet loyal and the root must not be shaken.

When Yingzhou was pacified, Yingzhou debated moving the capital to Xiakou; Chen again remonstrated firmly that Ba and the Gorges were not yet subdued and one should not lightly abandon the root and shake the people's hearts.
郢州平 means Yingzhou was pacified, not that 'Ying fell'; 穎胄議 is the person Yingzhou proposing the move; and 固諫…未賓…不宜輕舍根本，搖動民志 is fully restored in the proposed idiomatic.
His uncle Zuzheng, late in Song, was director of the imperial clan.
His uncle Zuzheng, late in Song, was chamberlain for attendants.
光祿勳 is Chamberlain for Attendants; director of the imperial clan would be 宗正, which is not in the Chinese.
His father's elder brother Zuzheng, at the end of Song, was Director of the Imperial Clan.
His father's elder brother Zuzheng, at the end of Song, was Chamberlain for Attendants.
Same office error: 光祿勳 is Chamberlain for Attendants, not Director of the Imperial Clan.
Then his brother-in-law Wang Cheng and cousin Du Heng were famed in the district.
Then his brother-in-law Wang Cheng and cousin Du Yun were famed in the district.
杜惲 is Du Yun (惲 = yùn); Heng is a wrong romanization of the same graph.
At the time Rui's brother-in-law Wang Cheng and cousin Du Heng both enjoyed great local fame.
At the time Rui's brother-in-law Wang Cheng and cousin Du Yun both enjoyed great local fame.
Literal likewise misreads 惲 as Heng; Yun is the correct reading.
Zuzheng asked Rui, "How do you think you compare to Cheng and Heng?"
Zuzheng asked Rui, "How do you think you compare to Cheng and Yun?"
Dialogue 憕、惲 repeats the same personal name 惲; it must be Yun, not Heng.
Zuzheng said to Rui: "How do you rate yourself beside Cheng and Heng?"
Zuzheng said to Rui: "How do you rate yourself beside Cheng and Yun?"
Same dialogue name 惲 requires Yun in the literal quotation.
The eastern palace rose; he became right commandant of the crown prince's guard, then left office as general who assists the state, inspector of Yuzhou, and administrator of Liyang.
The eastern palace rose; he became right commandant of the crown prince's guard, then went out as general who assists the state, inspector of Yuzhou, and administrator of Liyang.
出爲輔國將軍、豫州刺史 marks an outward provincial appointment; 'left office as' reverses 出爲.
In Song's first Yongguang year Yuan Yan held Yongzhou; he saw Rui, marveled, and made him chief clerk.
In Song's first Yongguang year Yuan Yan was Inspector of Yongzhou; he saw Rui, marveled, and made him chief clerk.
爲雍州刺史 names the office Inspector of Yongzhou; 'held Yongzhou' drops 刺史 present in the Chinese.
His third son Ling knew the classics and histories especially well and was called broadly learned. Rui always had Ling lecture on books; points Ling raised Rui could not match.

His third son Ling knew the classics and histories especially well and was called broadly learned. Rui always seated Ling and had him lecture on books; the points Rui raised, Ling still could not match.
叡每坐棱使說書 seats Ling to lecture, but 其所發擿，稜猶弗之逮也 makes Rui the raiser of points Ling still could not equal; the idiomatic had reversed agent and patient.

His third son Ling was especially versed in the classics and histories; the age called him broadly learned. Rui would seat Ling whenever he lectured on books; the points Ling raised, Rui still could not match.

His third son Ling was especially versed in the classics and histories; the age called him broadly learned. Rui would seat Ling and have him explain the books; the points Rui raised, Ling still could not match.
The literal likewise reversed 其所發擿，稜猶弗之逮也; Rui raised the points Ling could not match.
Gaozu sent Palace Secretary Zhou She to labor the army on the Huai; Rui piled the spoils at the camp gate for him to see. She looked and said to Rui, "Your capture here rivals Bear-Ear Mountain.

Gaozu sent Palace Secretary Zhou She to reward and comfort the army on the Huai; Rui piled the spoils at the camp gate for him to see. She looked and said to Rui, "Your capture here rivals Bear-Ear Mountain."
勞於淮上 is 勞軍, rewarding/comforting the troops, not making them labor; the proposed literal also closes the quotation.

At Shaoyang, Chang Yizhi greatly admired Rui and asked Cao Jingzong to meet him; they wagered two hundred thousand cash. Jingzong threw pheasant; Rui slowly threw black, flipped one piece, said "Strange!" and forced a tie.

At Shaoyang, Chang Yizhi was deeply grateful to Rui and asked Cao Jingzong to meet him; they wagered two hundred thousand cash. Jingzong threw pheasant; Rui slowly threw black, flipped one piece, said "Strange!" and forced a tie.
甚德叡 means Chang Yizhi felt deep gratitude toward Rui, not mere admiration.
Jing built east and west earthen mounds outside the wall and matching mounds within; the Lamenting Heir Apparent and those below carried earth with shovel and basket.

Jing built east and west earthen mounds outside the wall and matching mounds within; Taizong personally carried earth, and the Lamenting Heir Apparent and those below him carried earth with shovel and basket.
Idiomatic omitted 太宗親自負土 before 哀太子以下躬執畚鍤; the repair restores Taizong's personal labor.

At that time Jing raised east and west earthen mounds outside the wall, and within the city others were built to match; the Lamenting Heir Apparent and those below him personally carried earth, shovel and basket in hand.

At that time Jing raised east and west earthen mounds outside the wall, and within the city others were built to match; Taizong personally carried earth, and the Lamenting Heir Apparent and those below him personally took shovel and basket in hand.
Literal likewise dropped 太宗親自負土; restoring it correctly separates Taizong from the heir and those below.
His great-grandfather Guang was Jin Rear Army General and administrator of Beiping.
His great-great-grandfather Guang was Jin Rear Army General and administrator of Beiping.
高祖父 is the fourth-generation paternal ancestor (great-great-grandfather); great-grandfather would be 曾祖, which names Gui in the next sentence.
His great-grandfather Guang was Jin Rear Army General and Administrator of Beiping.
His great-great-grandfather Guang was Jin Rear Army General and Administrator of Beiping.
Same kinship grade: 高祖父 is great-great-grandfather, not great-grandfather.
His grandfather Gui, at the start of Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan era, moved south to Xiangyang, became the province's Separate Cart, then Regular Attendant.
His great-grandfather Gui, at the start of Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan era, moved south to Xiangyang, became the province's Separate Cart, then Regular Attendant.
曾祖軌 is great-grandfather; 祖公循 in the following unit is the grandfather, so 'grandfather Gui' collapses two generations.
His grandfather Gui, at the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan era, moved south to Xiangyang and became the province's Separate Cart, then Regular Attendant.
His great-grandfather Gui, at the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan era, moved south to Xiangyang and became the province's Separate Cart, then Regular Attendant.
Literal same error: 曾祖 is great-grandfather, not grandfather.
His son Ganxiang rose to General of Valiant Cavalry, chief clerk on the northern expedition, and administrator of Yiyang and Zhongli.
His son Ganxiang rose to General of Valiant Cavalry, chief clerk on the northern expedition, and administrator of Ruyin and Zhongli.
汝陰 is Ruyin; Yiyang (弋陽) is a different commandery not present in 汝陰、鐘離二郡太守.
His son Ganxiang rose in office to General of Valiant Cavalry, Chief Clerk of the Army on the Northern Expedition, and Administrator of the two commanderies of Yiyang and Zhongli.
His son Ganxiang rose in office to General of Valiant Cavalry, Chief Clerk of the Army on the Northern Expedition, and Administrator of the two commanderies of Ruyin and Zhongli.
Literal likewise misrenders 汝陰 as Yiyang; Ruyin is required.
